title: Segmenting for spelling
examples: Can you help me sound out the word cat?
How do I break down a word into sounds?
What does segmenting mean for spelling?

explain.say: listen carefully to this word. it is the word dog. say it with me. dog.
we are going to stretch the word out. we say /d/ /o/ /g/. we stretch it like this. /d/ /o/ /g/.
now we count how many sounds we hear. one sound for /d/, two sounds for /o/, three sounds for /g/. we say three sounds.
next we write each sound we hear. we write a letter for /d/, then a letter for /o/, and a letter for /g/. we write d, o, g.
A common mistake is thinking that the number of letters tells you the number of sounds. The letters are just the shapes we use to write the sounds. We must listen closely to hear each separate sound.

faq.a: Segmenting means breaking a word into its small sounds. It helps us hear each sound one by one. You might also hear this called sounding out.
asks: How do I sound out a word?
What does it mean to break a word apart?

faq.q: How do I know how many sounds there are?
faq.a: You tap your fingers for every sound you hear in the word. For example, the word sun has three sounds. You can try tapping it out.
asks: Can I count the sounds in a word?

faq.q: Do I write the letters or the sounds?
faq.a: We write the letters that match each sound you hear. For the sound /m/, we write the letter m. We match one sound to one letter.
asks: Do I write the letters or the sounds?
If I hear /s/, what letter do I write?

faq.q: Is this the same as blending?
faq.a: No, blending is putting sounds together to make a word. Segmenting is taking a word apart into its separate sounds. They are opposite skills.
asks: Is this the same as putting sounds together?
What is the difference between segmenting and blending?

faq.q: What if the word has a tricky sound?
faq.a: If a sound is tricky, like the 'ee' sound, you still count it as one sound. You just need to listen very carefully for that one sound.
asks: How do I count tricky sounds?

facts: Segmenting is breaking a word into its individual sounds.
We use our ears to hear the sounds when segmenting.
Each sound usually matches one letter or a small group of letters.
This skill helps us learn to spell words correctly.

quiz.say: What is the first step when segmenting the word 'cup'?

options.show: Writing the letters c, u, p.
options.say: Writing the letters c, u, p.

options.show: Counting the total number of letters.
options.say: Counting the total number of letters.

quiz.why: Stretching the word helps you hear each sound separately.

wrong.0: We need to slow down to hear every single sound.
wrong.2: This is the last step, not the first one.
wrong.3: We count the sounds, not just the letters.

quiz.say: If you hear the word 'mat', how many sounds do you count?
quiz.why: You can hear /m/, /a/, and /t/, which is three separate sounds.

wrong.0: You are adding an extra sound that is not there.
wrong.2: You are missing the sound at the end of the word.
wrong.3: The word has three distinct sounds you can hear.

quiz.say: When you segment the word 'sit', what letters do you write?
quiz.why: You write one letter for each sound you hear: /s/, /i/, /t/.

wrong.0: You wrote an extra letter for the middle sound.
wrong.1: You put two sounds together when you should separate them.
wrong.2: You added an extra letter that does not make a sound.
